title: How Transformers Work
subtitle: Attention, embeddings, and the transformer architecture

content.text: Transformers use self-attention to process all tokens in parallel and weigh their relevance to each other.

content.definition: A mechanism that lets each token look at all other tokens and decide which are most relevant for predicting the next token.
A dense vector representation of a token or text. Similar meanings have similar vectors.

content.code:
# Embeddings via API
import anthropic
client = anthropic.Anthropic()

# Most providers offer an embeddings endpoint
# for semantic similarity and vector search
from openai import OpenAI
oai = OpenAI()

response = oai.embeddings.create(
    input="Machine learning is transforming industries",
    model="text-embedding-3-small"
)
vector = response.data[0].embedding  # list of 1536 floats

content.text: You do not need to understand transformer internals to build great LLM applications, but it helps to understand why models have context limits and why longer contexts cost more.

questions.question: What does self-attention allow a transformer to do?
options: Process tokens one at a time
Weight every token against every other token in the sequence
questions.explanation: Self-attention computes how relevant each token is to every other token in the input sequence.

faq.q: What is the difference between GPT and BERT?
faq.a: GPT is a decoder-only model (generates text left-to-right). BERT is encoder-only (understands full context). GPT-style models power most chat LLMs.
